title: A Table With Two Columns
dek: A page registry is a table: a shape name that appears in your data on the left, the code allowed to draw it on the right. This is a working design for that table — the three shapes a page can have, six ways to build the lookup, what one entry must carry, where to validate, how to version against two clocks, and the failure modes that arrive on schedule. Then a section on doing it with MagicPath, grounded in its CLI rather than its marketing, with an honest ledger of what that buys and what it costs.
byline: 28 September 2026 · Synthesised from published engineering write-ups and vendor docs; the MagicPath section is grounded in CLI output produced here
description: How to build a registry of pages that renders documents dynamically from their shape — schema, resolver, registry, renderer — and how MagicPath fits, with pros and cons.
og_description: A page registry maps a shape name in your data to the code allowed to draw it. This essay works through the three shapes a page can have, six registry strategies from an object literal to a typed cross-platform transport, the ten fields one registry entry should carry, four places to validate, versioning against two deploy clocks, the React Server Components bundle trap, and the failure modes that arrive on schedule — then wires MagicPath in as a block factory and prices the trade.
